name: Dell Technologies Inc.
industry: Technology Hardware / IT Infrastructure / AI Servers
title: Dell Technologies — Michael Dell's AI server franchise at $113.5B revenue and a $43B backlog
subtitle: From a 1984 University of Texas dorm room to the post-EMC consolidation, the 2018 VMware-tracking-stock relisting, the 2023 ISG-driven AI server cycle, and the FY2026 $24.6B AI server quarter — how the most operationally complex US technology company runs at scale
abstract: Dell Technologies Inc. (DELL, NYSE) is the integrated technology hardware and infrastructure platform built around the 1984 founding company of the same name, now Chairman and CEO Michael Dell's franchise at $113.5 billion of FY2026 revenue (fiscal year ended approximately January 30 2026) and approximately $43 billion of AI server backlog entering FY2027. The company operates two reportable segments: Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) — servers, storage, networking, AI Factory — which generated $18.82 billion in Q4 FY26 (+66% YoY) on the back of $24.6 billion of full-year AI server revenue (+300%+ YoY) and over $64 billion of AI-optimised server orders closed during FY26 with $25+ billion of AI server shipments; and Client Solutions Group (CSG) — commercial and consumer PCs — which generated $13.5 billion in Q4 (+14% YoY) with commercial $11.6 billion (+16%) and consumer $1.9 billion (flat). The executive bench combines Michael Dell as Chairman and CEO with Jeff Clarke as Vice Chairman and COO (running CSG, ISG, and Global Supply Chain since December 2019), Chuck Whitten as the post-Bain joined-2021 commercial co-leader, Bill Scannell as global sales leader (30+ years at Dell), and David Kennedy as interim CFO from September 2025 following Yvonne McGill's announced transition (after nearly 30 years at Dell including CFO since 2023; remains in advisory capacity through Q3 fiscal 2026). The board is anchored by Michael Dell as Chairman alongside Ellen Kullman (Lead Independent Director, ex-DuPont CEO, Carbon Inc. Executive Chair), Egon Durban (Silver Lake Co-CEO, board since October 2013), David Dorman (Founding Partner Centerview Capital Technology), William Green (ex-Accenture Chairman, Audit Committee Chair), David Grain (Grain Management founder/CEO), Steven Mollenkopf (ex-Qualcomm CEO), and Lynn Vojvodich Radakovich. The board has unanimously recommended Dell's redomestication to Texas. The investment proposition compresses the AI server demand cycle, customer-supply alignment with Nvidia + AMD + hyperscaler buyers, AI PC refresh cycle in CSG, and the operating-leverage opportunity as the ISG mix shifts toward AI server revenue — against execution risk on the $43B backlog ramp, AI capex cyclicality, and competition from HPE / Supermicro / Lenovo / direct hyperscaler ODMs.
